title: Property tax relief for a disabled Veteran, paid as a reimbursement
summary: Tennessee does not exempt your home. It reimburses you from state funds for property taxes on the first $175,000 of market value. You still get a bill and you are still responsible for it, and unlike the elderly and disabled programmes there is no income limit.
amount: Reimbursement calculated on the first $175,000 of full market value, which at the statutory 25 percent ratio is $43,750 of effective assessed value, multiplied by your adjusted local tax rate
eligibility: You served in the armed forces of the United States, and you own and use the property as your residence

And you acquired in connection with that service a disability from paraplegia or permanent paralysis of both legs and the lower part of the body resulting from traumatic injury or disease to the spinal cord or brain, or from legal blindness, or from loss or loss of use of two or more limbs from any service-connected cause
Or you acquired a 100 percent permanent total disability as determined by the VA, that disability resulting from having served as a prisoner of war
Or you acquired a service-connected permanent and total disability as determined by the VA
Relief never extends to anyone dishonorably discharged from any of the armed services
You must complete form F-16, a consent form releasing disability and income information from the VA. A surviving spouse completes form F-16S
details: Understand the mechanism before anything else, because the word relief is doing a lot of work here. This is not an exemption. The state pays or reimburses you for all or part of the local property taxes you paid for the year. You still receive your tax bill and you are still responsible for paying it. When you are approved you get a voucher with your tax bill, which you present to the collecting official before the deadline along with payment of any balance due.

There is no income test in this section. The elderly and disabled homeowner programmes cap income, at $38,470 for the 2026 programme year, and cap the relieved market value at $33,600. Neither cap applies to a disabled Veteran, whose ceiling is $175,000 of market value. If you qualify as a disabled Veteran, this is the route to take, and the statute says the payment is in lieu of anything under the elderly or disabled sections rather than in addition.

The arithmetic is defined. Effective assessed value is the full market value up to $175,000 multiplied by 25 percent. That is then multiplied by a tax rate adjusted to reflect the relationship between appraised and market value in your jurisdiction, as determined by the State Board of Equalization. Full market value itself is your appraised value adjusted by the same relationship. So two Veterans with identically appraised homes in different counties can receive different amounts.

A deadline point where the state's own documents disagree, so we are giving you both. The statute says that a taxpayer who fails to apply or present a credit voucher within thirty-five days from the date taxes become delinquent is ineligible for that year, and then says expressly that nothing in that provision requires the full amount of taxes to be paid by the delinquency date as a condition of eligibility. The Comptroller's 2026 brochure states that taxes must also be paid by that date. Treat the thirty-five day filing deadline as firm, and ask the tax relief office before assuming you must clear the whole bill first.

There is a second backstop date. Applications and voucher presentments are valid only if received in the Division of Property Assessments by 5 May following the last date they may be made, or within thirty days of the thirty-five day deadline, whichever is later.

If you missed a deadline, ask anyway. The director of the Division of Property Assessments can waive any deadline in the section on determining that the failure was excusable for good and reasonable cause, though no deadline can be extended past 31 December of the year following the tax year.

Ask your county and your city whether they top it up. Counties, municipalities and metropolitan governments may appropriate their own funds for additional relief for disabled Veterans, capped so that state and local relief together never exceed the taxes actually paid. You have to have applied for and obtained the state relief first. This is money a lot of Veterans leave on the table.

A provision worth knowing before you need it. You continue to qualify while temporarily relocated for health care to the home of a friend or relative, or to a hospital or a skilled or intermediate care facility, as long as you indicate an intent to return to the residence when recovered sufficiently.

Surviving spouses have three separate routes. A spouse of a disabled Veteran who was eligible at the time of death qualifies, and so does the spouse where a later amendment to the eligibility rules would have made the deceased Veteran eligible, which is unusually generous. Separately, the spouse of a Veteran whose death resulted from a service-connected combat-related cause qualifies, as does the spouse of a soldier whose death resulted from being deployed away from any home base of training in support of combat or peace operations. All three require that the spouse does not remarry, owns the property solely or jointly, and uses it exclusively as a home.
The VA's determination of your disability status is conclusive for this section, so the argument about your rating happens with the VA and not with Tennessee.
Your disability information is confidential and is not subject to inspection under Tennessee public records law, though it is available to the officials who administer or audit the programme.

You can only receive relief on your primary residence, one property per year. An irrevocable trust defeats the claim, because the property is owned by the trust. Your spouse's income and signature are required for the elderly and disabled routes regardless of residency or ownership, so expect to be asked. State checks are not forwarded, so tell the collecting official about address changes and long absences.
Apply through your county trustee, or your city collecting official if the property is inside city limits. The state tax relief office is on 615-747-8871 or 1-800-221-9927, and TRInfo@cot.tn.gov.

On the source, and it is a good news story. Arkansas and Mississippi make you go through a commercial vendor to read their statutes. Tennessee's Comptroller publishes the text of these four sections directly, as a PDF on a tn.gov address, which is what this record is built on and what the official link points to. The 2026 figures come from the Comptroller's own tax relief brochure.
agency: County trustees and city collecting officials, administered by the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury Division of Property Assessments
statuteRef: Tenn. Code Ann. 67-5-704, with administration, deadlines and local top-up relief at 67-5-701

title: Military retirement pay is not taxed, because there is no income tax
summary: Tennessee has no state income tax on earned income or retirement pay. The one income tax it had, the Hall tax, only ever reached interest and dividends, and it was repealed for tax periods beginning on or after 1 January 2021.
eligibility: No application, exemption or claim is required, because there is no tax to be exempt from
This applies to military retired pay, VA compensation, active and reserve component pay and civilian earnings alike
details: The Hall income tax is the reason you will still see Tennessee described as having an income tax in older guidance. It was enacted in 1929 and named after the senator who sponsored it, and it was imposed only on individuals and entities receiving interest from bonds and notes and dividends from stock. It never reached wages or retirement pay.
It was repealed for tax periods that begin on 1 January 2021 or later. The Department of Revenue's instruction is explicit: do not file a return for any tax year beginning on or after that date.

So a Veteran moving to Tennessee is not looking for a military retirement exemption, a cap or an age threshold. There is nothing to claim. Any guidance telling you to subtract military retirement on a Tennessee return is describing a tax that no longer exists.
Tennessee still levies plenty of other taxes, including property tax, which is where the Veteran-specific relief in this state sits. See the property tax relief record.
